# Medical Doctor/Intern SOP This is the list of procedures, responsibilities, and duties of the [color=#42636d][bold]Medical Doctor[/bold][/color] and [color=#42636d][bold]Medical Intern[/bold][/color] of this station.
1. Though not mandatory, it is recommended that Medical Doctors wear Sterile Masks/internals and Latex/Nitrile gloves when handling patients. This Guideline becomes mandatory during Viral Outbreaks [bold]and[/bold] when performing [bold][italic]Surgeries[/italic][/bold].
2. Medical Interns should focus on tending to patients that require light care and helping other qualified Medical staff in whatever they require. If necessary, they may stand in for regular Medical Doctor duties.3. Medical Doctors must ensure there is at least one (1) Defibrillator charged and available for use in the Exam Room (or wherever the main treatment area may be). 4. Medical Doctors must maintain the entirety of Medbay in a hygienic state. This includes (but is not limited to) cleaning organic residue, fluids, and/or corpses. Janitorial Services should be requested for major spills. 5. Medical Doctors must place all corpses inside body bags and/or freezers to preserve their state when unable to be worked on immediately. In extreme overload, the morgue may be used for preservation but should be checked for [bold][italic]souls[/italic][/bold] to ensure bodies can be revived. 6. Medical Doctors, in conjunction with other Medical staff, must ensure that Cloning is stocked with sufficient Biomass for at least one patient at any given time. Additional Biomass may be stored in a Medical Biofabricator until needed. In addition, Medical Doctors must make sure that the Morgue does not contain cloneable corpses.
7. Medical Doctors must certify that all cloned personnel are properly transferred to the new cloned body. In addition, Medical Doctors must ensure cloned personnel are fully healed and any damage or missing organs are fixed before release.8. Medical Doctors are not permitted to leave Medbay to perform recreational activities if there are unattended patients requiring treatment. 9.Medical Doctors should take patients to surgery if they have severe localised brute, burn and/or bone damage. 10. Medical Doctors are not obligated to treat patients who are actively and intentionally harming themselves. If treated, refer the patient to the on-station [color=#42636d][bold]Psychologist[/bold][/color] if one is present.
11. In the case that there is no [color=#42636d][bold]Virologist[/bold][/color] on station and a Viral Outbreak occurs, available Medical Doctors are allowed to assume the duties of a Virologist until one arrives or the Viral Outbreak has been eradicated.
